input.strategy_title: Default Vector Store for Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag
input.strategy_markdown:
## Summary

RHOAI must provide a default vector store that is available out-of-the-box — without manual setup — so that Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag continue to function when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution image. Today these capabilities depend on an inline vector store provider bundled within the Llama Stack process; removing it (per RHAISTRAT-7474) will break them unless an alternative is available at the platform level.

## Problem Statement

Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag currently rely on an inline Milvus provider embedded in the Llama Stack distribution image to store and retrieve vector embeddings. This inline provider runs inside the Llama Stack process itself.

RHAISTRAT-7474 proposes removing inline providers from the Llama Stack distribution to improve GA readiness — shipping only what can be tested and maintained at scale, and aligning with Llama Stack's primary use case as a remote API server. However, no platform-level alternative exists today. If inline providers are removed without a replacement, any RHOAI user relying on Gen AI Studio's RAG capabilities or Auto Rag will lose functionality entirely — there is no workaround short of manually provisioning and configuring an external vector database.

Users expect vector storage to "just work" when they use Gen AI Studio or Auto Rag. The current out-of-the-box experience must be preserved even as the underlying architecture evolves.

## Affected Customers

* All RHOAI customers using Gen AI Studio playground with RAG capabilities
* All RHOAI customers using Auto Rag
* This is a platform-level product dependency: these features cannot function without a vector store

## Business Justification

* **Product integrity:** Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag are GA-track capabilities in RHOAI. Removing the inline vector store without a replacement breaks shipped product functionality for every user of these features.
* **Blocking dependency:** RHAISTRAT-7474 (removing inline providers for GA readiness) cannot proceed until this RFE is resolved. Silas Brenmark (Gen AI Studio lead) has identified this as a blocker.
* **User experience:** RHOAI differentiates on integrated, opinionated defaults. Requiring users to manually provision and configure a vector database before they can use the playground or Auto Rag degrades the out-of-the-box experience that customers expect from the platform.

## Acceptance Criteria

* \[ \] A default vector store is available out-of-the-box on RHOAI without requiring users to manually provision or configure external infrastructure
* \[ \] Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] Auto Rag functions with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] The default vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the Llama Stack instance (not an inline provider)
* \[ \] The default vector store is scoped appropriately for multi-tenant environments (e.g., per-namespace isolation)
* \[ \] The default vector store is lightweight enough to run in resource-constrained environments without imposing significant overhead

## Success Criteria

* Users of Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag experience no functional regression when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution
* No additional manual setup steps are required for RAG workflows compared to the current experience
* RHAISTRAT-7474 is unblocked and can proceed to implementation

## Open Questions

* What is the preferred scoping model — per namespace, per Llama Stack instance, or both? (Silas noted per-namespace is preferred for isolation, but Auto Rag may need per-instance scoping)
* Should users have a migration path from the default vector store to a production-grade vector database? (Bram Sundqvist raised the importance of aligning with commonly-used vector DB providers for easier migration)

## Strategy (AI Generated by Agentic SDLC Pipeline)

> **Note:** The full strategy exceeds Jira's description size limit and is stored as an attachment: `RHAISTRAT-8004-strategy.md`.

## Staff Engineer Input

**Correction 1 — OGX does not auto-provision PostgreSQL.** OGX defaults to SQLite for storage (`storage.kv.type: sqlite`, `storage.sql.type: sqlite` in the OGXServer CRD). The odh-dashboard gen-ai BFF hardcodes SQLite when creating OGXServer instances for the playground (`kv_sqlite` and `sql_sqlite` in `llamastack_config.go`). PostgreSQL is a supported backend but must be user-configured with an explicit `connectionString` secret. The strategy's claim that "every LlamaStackDistribution instance requires a PostgreSQL database" is incorrect — introducing PostgreSQL is new work, not an extension of existing infrastructure.

**Correction 2 — A Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector already exists.** The `registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16` image includes pgvector out of the box — confirmed in the [sclorg/postgresql-container Dockerfile](https://github.com/sclorg/postgresql-container/blob/master/16/Dockerfile.rhel9) (`INSTALL_PKGS="$INSTALL_PKGS pgvector"`). PostgreSQL 18 (RHEL 9) also includes pgvector. Furthermore, the model-registry-operator already uses `postgresql-16` as its auto-provisioned database image, and `RELATED_IMAGE_POSTGRESQL_16_IMAGE` is already present in the rhods-operator CSV for disconnected installs. No custom image build is needed. No Konflux onboarding is needed. The 1-2 sprint image onboarding estimate in the strategy can be eliminated.

**Architectural direction — platform-level database vs. self-provisioned.** Multiple RHOAI components now need PostgreSQL (model-registry, MLflow, and now OGX for pgvector). The preferred long-term direction is a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL managed via the DSC, where each component consumes a connection string rather than self-provisioning. A shared platform-provided PostgreSQL via DSC will not be available until RHOAI 3.6. For 3.5, Gen AI Studio must provision its own PostgreSQL instance.

**Operator dependency for self-provisioning (RHAISTRAT-7164).** Self-provisioning PostgreSQL following the model-registry-operator pattern requires a RHOAI-controlled operator for Gen AI Studio. The ogx-k8s-operator is upstream and cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning logic. The dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress) would provide this operator layer. This is a hard dependency — until RHAISTRAT-7164 delivers, there is no RHOAI-controlled operator where PostgreSQL lifecycle management can live. It will be challenging to commit this strategy to a specific release until that dependency is delivered.

**Fallback if RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time.** If the dashboard modularization is not ready for 3.5, the fallback is to require customers to bring their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities in the Playground. Users would manually configure the OGXServer CR spec with their PostgreSQL connection details. This aligns with the breaking changes introduced in OGX 1.0, even though the Playground largely abstracts OGX from users. The development team should define a go/no-go gate for this decision as part of sprint planning.

**Decouple from Auto Rag.** Auto Rag integration with Gen AI Studio (RHAISTRAT-7824) is targeting RHOAI 3.6. This strategy should validate pgvector only for Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows. Auto Rag compatibility with pgvector will be addressed in RHAISTRAT-7824's scope. Remove Auto Rag from affected components, impacted teams, acceptance criteria, and validation requirements.

**Performance and index thresholds — dev experimentation scope.** The default pgvector instance is meant for development experimentation, not production usage. Strict latency SLAs (p50/p95/p99) are not required. The sprint 1 benchmark should capture the inline Milvus baseline and verify pgvector is in the same order of magnitude, not meet a specific threshold. Typical Playground RAG usage involves small document sets — flat scan (no index) is sufficient for the default. Users with production-scale vector workloads should use an external vector database. Remove open questions about latency thresholds, corpus size ranges, and index type selection.

**PostgreSQL resource sizing.** Reference the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource requests/limits as the starting point. Adjust based on sprint 1 benchmarking if needed.

**Alternative fallback — BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning.** If RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time, an alternative to requiring customers to bring their own PostgreSQL is to have the gen-ai BFF provision the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly, similar to how the BFF currently provisions guardrails infrastructure. The BFF would create the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret when a playground with RAG is configured, if one does not already exist in the namespace. Caveats: (1) the implementation must be designed for portability — when the platform-provided shared database becomes available (3.6), the BFF should consume the shared connection string rather than self-provisioning; (2) lifecycle management of the PostgreSQL instance must be carefully considered — the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, so cleanup on playground deletion, handling of pod restarts, and credential rotation need explicit design attention.

**Existing remote vector store implementation is reusable.** Per the engineering team, the existing remote vector store implementation can be largely reused for pgvector integration. The majority of the work effort is around infrastructure and provisioning of the PostgreSQL/pgvector database, not the vector_io provider integration itself.

**Correction 3 — Vector storage and application storage are independent configurations.** The OGX vector_io provider configuration (`remote::pgvector` via `ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) is completely separate from OGX's application storage backend configuration (`storage.kv.type`, `storage.sql.type`). This strategy only needs to configure the pgvector vector_io provider — it does not change the application storage backend, which remains on its existing default (SQLite). There is no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration concern because the application storage is not being touched. Remove any references to consolidating vector and application storage in a single database, and remove any SQLite-to-PostgreSQL upgrade path considerations.

# Operator-managed PostgreSQL/pgvector provisioning for Gen AI Studio (path A)

## Description

Conditional branch A of the default-vector-store strategy, executed if the
RHOAI 3.5 provisioning-path go/no-go decision selects the operator-managed
path — i.e. the RHOAI-controlled operator layer for Gen AI Studio (delivered
by RHAISTRAT-7164, dashboard operator modularization) is available in time.
This epic implements PostgreSQL-with-pgvector lifecycle management in that
operator layer, following the established model-registry-operator pattern for
auto-provisioned databases, so that a default vector store is available
out-of-the-box wherever a Gen AI Studio playground with RAG is configured.
No custom image build is needed: the Red Hat `postgresql-16` image already
includes pgvector and is already referenced by the platform for disconnected
installs.

## Scope

- Implement per-namespace PostgreSQL instance lifecycle management (create,
  configure, clean up) in the RHOAI-controlled operator layer delivered by
  RHAISTRAT-7164, following the model-registry-operator's auto-provisioning
  pattern for PostgreSQL (the upstream ogx-k8s-operator cannot carry this
  RHOAI-specific logic).
- Provision one instance per namespace where a Gen AI Studio playground with
  RAG is configured (per-namespace scoping for multi-tenant isolation).
- Use the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL image that ships pgvector
  (`registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16`); reference it through the
  platform's related-image mechanism so disconnected installs work.
- Set initial resource requests/limits from the model-registry-operator's
  PostgreSQL sizing as the starting point.
- Publish the connection details as a secret in the namespace, consumable by
  the playground's OGXServer vector_io provider configuration (integration
  with that configuration is a configuration reference — the playground
  wiring is validated by acceptance criteria, not a build-time dependency).
- Remove the provisioned instance when no playground in the namespace
  requires it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a Gen AI Studio playground with RAG is configured in a namespace, the
  operator layer provisions a PostgreSQL instance with pgvector in that
  namespace, with no manual user setup or external infrastructure
  configuration.
- The provisioned instance's connection details are published as a secret in
  the namespace that the playground's OGXServer pgvector vector_io
  configuration consumes, and an end-to-end playground RAG workflow
  (ingest, retrieve, chat) functions against it.
- Resource requests/limits on the provisioned instance start from the
  model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL sizing.
- The image reference resolves on disconnected installs (via the platform's
  related-image mechanism for the PostgreSQL 16 image).
- The instance is removed when no playground in the namespace requires a
  vector store (no orphaned deployments after playground removal).
- Per-namespace isolation: each namespace gets its own instance; no
  cross-namespace data access.

## HLR Traceability

- **AC-1 (P0): default vector store available out-of-the-box without manual
  provisioning or configuration of external infrastructure** — this branch is
  one of the two conditional implementations of that requirement.
- **AC-2 (P0): playground RAG workflows function with the default vector
  store with no loss of current capability** — end-to-end functional
  acceptance criteria above (independent validation is carried by the
  strategy's validation-and-benchmark epic).
- **AC-4 (P1): scoped appropriately for multi-tenant environments
  (per-namespace isolation)** — implemented by the per-namespace provisioning
  model.

# BFF-managed PostgreSQL/pgvector provisioning for Gen AI Studio playgrounds (path B)

## Description

Conditional branch B of the default-vector-store strategy, executed if the
RHOAI 3.5 provisioning-path go/no-go decision selects the BFF-managed path —
i.e. the RHOAI-controlled operator layer from RHAISTRAT-7164 is not available
in time for 3.5. This epic has the gen-ai BFF provision the
PostgreSQL-with-pgvector instance directly, similar to how the BFF already
provisions guardrails infrastructure: when a playground with RAG is
configured and no suitable instance exists in the namespace, the BFF creates
the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret. Because the BFF is not
an operator with a reconciliation loop, lifecycle management (cleanup on
playground deletion, pod-restart recovery, credential rotation) receives
explicit design attention, and the implementation is designed for
portability to the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL planned for a later
RHOAI release.

## Scope

- Implement BFF-managed provisioning: when a playground with RAG is
  configured, create the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret in
  the namespace if no suitable instance already exists (per-namespace
  scoping; idempotent creation that reuses an existing instance).
- Use the existing Red Hat PostgreSQL image that ships pgvector
  (`registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16`); reference it through the
  platform's related-image mechanism so disconnected installs work.
- Design and implement lifecycle handling appropriate to a non-operator
  controller: cleanup when the playground is deleted, recovery from
  PostgreSQL pod restarts, and a documented approach to credential rotation.
- Design for portability: when the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL
  becomes available (planned RHOAI 3.6), the BFF consumes the shared
  connection string instead of self-provisioning — the provisioning decision
  must be isolatable behind a connection-resolution step.
- Set initial resource requests/limits from the model-registry-operator's
  PostgreSQL sizing as the starting point.
- Wire the provisioned connection secret into the playground's OGXServer
  pgvector vector_io provider configuration delivered by this strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a Gen AI Studio playground with RAG is configured in a namespace with
  no existing suitable PostgreSQL instance, the BFF creates the Deployment,
  Service, PVC, and Secret for a pgvector-enabled PostgreSQL instance, with
  no manual user setup.
- Provisioning is idempotent: an existing suitable instance in the namespace
  is reused, not duplicated; playgrounds in the same namespace share one
  instance (per-namespace isolation).
- An end-to-end playground RAG workflow (ingest, retrieve, chat) functions
  against the BFF-provisioned store via the pgvector vector_io provider
  configuration.
- Lifecycle behavior is implemented and tested: the provisioned resources
  are cleaned up when the playground is deleted, the playground recovers
  from a PostgreSQL pod restart, and the credential-rotation approach is
  documented and implemented.
- The connection-resolution step is isolatable: the design demonstrates
  swapping self-provisioning for a platform-provided shared connection
  string without rewriting the playground configuration surface.
- Resource requests/limits on the provisioned instance start from the
  model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL sizing.
- The image reference resolves on disconnected installs (via the platform's
  related-image mechanism for the PostgreSQL 16 image).

## HLR Traceability

- **AC-1 (P0): default vector store available out-of-the-box without manual
  provisioning or configuration of external infrastructure** — this branch is
  the fallback conditional implementation of that requirement when the
  operator layer is not available.
- **AC-2 (P0): playground RAG workflows function with the default vector
  store with no loss of current capability** — end-to-end functional
  acceptance criteria above (independent validation is carried by the
  strategy's validation-and-benchmark epic).
- **AC-4 (P1): scoped appropriately for multi-tenant environments
  (per-namespace isolation)** — implemented by the per-namespace
  create-if-absent provisioning model.

# Investigation: RHOAI 3.5 provisioning-path go/no-go for the default vector store

## Description

This investigation resolves the gating unknown in the default-vector-store
strategy: whether the RHOAI-controlled operator layer for Gen AI Studio —
delivered by RHAISTRAT-7164 (dashboard operator modularization, currently In
Progress) — will be available in time for RHOAI 3.5 to host PostgreSQL
lifecycle management. The outcome selects the provisioning path for the
default pgvector vector store and therefore determines which downstream
implementation work exists. Per the Staff Engineer Input, the development
team must define this go/no-go gate as part of sprint planning; this epic
produces that decision as a reviewable record.

## Scope

- Assess the delivery status and realistic landing date of RHAISTRAT-7164
  (dashboard operator modularization) against the RHOAI 3.5 release timeline,
  in consultation with the team delivering it.
- Confirm whether the delivered operator layer can carry RHOAI-specific
  PostgreSQL/pgvector provisioning logic (the upstream ogx-k8s-operator
  cannot).
- Decide the provisioning path for 3.5, selecting exactly one of:
  - **Path A — operator-managed**: PostgreSQL lifecycle management in the
    RHOAI-controlled operator layer, following the model-registry-operator
    pattern.
  - **Path B — BFF-managed**: the gen-ai BFF provisions the PostgreSQL
    instance directly (Deployment, Service, PVC, Secret), mirroring its
    existing guardrails-infrastructure provisioning.
- Record the final fallback if the selected path fails during implementation:
  requiring users to bring their own PostgreSQL by manually configuring the
  OGXServer CR spec (a degraded, non-out-of-the-box experience).
- Communicate the decision to the owner of RHAISTRAT-7474 (removal of inline
  providers), which is blocked by this strategy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written decision record exists that states whether the RHOAI-controlled
  operator layer will be available in time for RHOAI 3.5, citing the evidence
  (RHAISTRAT-7164 status and timeline assessment) used to reach the conclusion.
- The record selects exactly one provisioning path (operator-managed or
  BFF-managed) for 3.5 and names the decision date and decision owner
  consistent with the sprint-planning gate.
- The record documents the fallback to bring-your-own PostgreSQL and the
  conditions under which it would be invoked.
- The decision is communicated to the stakeholders of the inline-provider
  removal strategy (RHAISTRAT-7474) and to the Gen AI Studio team, and the
  selected path is reflected in the sprint plan.

## HLR Traceability

- **AC-1 (P0): default vector store available out-of-the-box** — this
  investigation gates both provisioning implementations that deliver AC-1;
  it is implicitly P0 because it blocks all P0 provisioning work.
- Supports the strategy's success criterion "RHAISTRAT-7474 is unblocked and
  can proceed to implementation" by fixing the provisioning direction.

# Enable the remote pgvector vector_io provider for Gen AI Studio playgrounds

## Description

This epic delivers the vector-store integration half of the default vector
store: the gen-ai BFF's creation of OGXServer instances for Gen AI Studio
playgrounds is extended to configure the remote pgvector vector_io provider
(activated via the `ENABLE_PGVECTOR` mechanism) instead of relying on the
inline Milvus provider bundled in the OGX distribution image. The existing
remote vector store implementation is largely reused — the engineering team
confirms the majority of the strategy's effort is infrastructure provisioning,
not provider integration. This configuration is needed regardless of which
party provisions the PostgreSQL database (operator layer or BFF), because in
every outcome the provider consumes a PostgreSQL connection secret.

## Scope

- Extend the gen-ai BFF's OGXServer instance creation (the playground
  configuration today hardcoding SQLite application storage in
  `llamastack_config.go`) to activate the remote pgvector vector_io provider
  for playgrounds with RAG enabled.
- Consume a PostgreSQL connection secret when one is present in the
  namespace, wiring it into the vector_io provider configuration (the
  interface shared with whichever provisioning approach is selected).
- Leave OGX application storage untouched: vector storage
  (`remote::pgvector`) and application storage (`storage.kv.type` /
  `storage.sql.type`, default SQLite) are independent configurations — no
  SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration is in scope.
- Per-namespace scoping: playgrounds in the same namespace share the default
  vector store instance.
- No OGX distribution code changes: the distribution already ships the remote
  pgvector vector_io backend (the ogx-distribution architecture context
  confirms PGVector is a supported backend and inline providers are stripped);
  only configuration emitted by the BFF changes.
- Ensure the configuration uses standard PostgreSQL connection semantics so a
  user can later point the same configuration at an external, production-grade
  vector database.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gen-ai BFF's OGXServer provisioning for playgrounds with RAG enabled
  activates the remote pgvector vector_io provider, so vector storage runs as
  a separate process decoupled from the OGX instance (not an inline provider).
- The provider configuration consumes a PostgreSQL connection secret present
  in the namespace; when no secret is present, behavior is defined and
  documented (no silent misconfiguration).
- OGX application storage remains on its existing default (SQLite); no
  application-storage migration is performed.
- The playground RAG configuration remains revertible to the current inline
  provider behavior (configuration rollback) until the inline-provider removal
  strategy (RHAISTRAT-7474) proceeds — the replacing capability ships with a
  rollback path.
- The vector_io connection configuration uses standard PostgreSQL connection
  semantics, allowing the same configuration surface to target an external
  production-grade vector database later.
- Unit and integration tests cover the OGXServer spec generation with the
  pgvector vector_io provider enabled, including the shared-namespace
  (per-namespace) scoping behavior.

## HLR Traceability

- **AC-2 (P0): Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the
  default vector store with no loss of current capability** — delivers the
  provider configuration those workflows run on (Auto Rag is out of scope per
  Staff Engineer Input; covered by RHAISTRAT-7824).
- **AC-3 (P0): the default vector store runs as a separate process,
  decoupled from the OGX instance (not an inline provider)** — delivered by
  configuring the remote pgvector provider.
- **OQ-2 (P2, bundled): migration path to a production-grade vector
  database** — bundled into this epic because migration readiness is a
  property of the same connection-configuration surface built here (standard
  PostgreSQL connection semantics); there is no separately schedulable
  migration deliverable in this release. The lower priority reads as relative
  value, not a deferral signal.

# Validate and benchmark Gen AI Studio playground RAG on the default pgvector store

## Description

This epic delivers the validation and benchmark evidence that the default
pgvector vector store preserves the out-of-the-box Gen AI Studio playground
RAG experience now that the inline Milvus provider is being removed from the
OGX distribution. It produces a benchmark report capturing the inline Milvus
baseline and verifying pgvector performs in the same order of magnitude on
representative playground-scale workloads, plus a functional no-regression
validation of playground RAG workflows, and a resource-sizing recommendation
for the provisioned PostgreSQL instance. Per the Staff Engineer Input, the
default store is scoped for development experimentation: no strict latency
SLAs (p50/p95/p99) apply, and typical playground usage involves small
document sets where a flat scan (no index) is sufficient.

## Scope

- Capture the inline Milvus baseline for current playground RAG workflows
  (document ingest, retrieval, chat with RAG) before inline providers are
  removed from the OGX distribution.
- Measure the same workflows against the default pgvector store provisioned
  by the selected provisioning path, on representative playground-scale
  document sets, and verify pgvector is within the same order of magnitude as
  the baseline (order-of-magnitude comparison, not a threshold gate).
- Functional no-regression validation: every playground RAG capability
  available today works unchanged against the default pgvector store, with no
  additional manual setup steps compared to the current experience.
- Validate per-namespace isolation behavior of the default store in a
  multi-tenant namespace layout.
- Produce a resource-sizing recommendation for the provisioned PostgreSQL
  instance, starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource
  requests/limits as the reference and adjusting based on the measurements.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A benchmark report exists that captures the inline Milvus baseline
  measurements and the pgvector measurements for the same playground RAG
  workloads, and states whether pgvector is within the same order of
  magnitude (with the raw numbers and methodology).
- The validation campaign runs against a default pgvector store provisioned
  by the selected provisioning path in a representative environment, and the
  report identifies which path was exercised.
- Functional no-regression validation passes: document ingest, retrieval, and
  chat-with-RAG workflows in the Gen AI Studio playground behave with no loss
  of current capability and no additional manual setup steps.
- Per-namespace isolation is verified: RAG data in one namespace is not
  visible to playgrounds in another namespace.
- A resource-sizing recommendation is produced (requests/limits for the
  provisioned PostgreSQL instance), referencing the model-registry-operator
  sizing as the starting point and any adjustments made from the benchmark
  data.

## HLR Traceability

- **AC-2 (P0): Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the
  default vector store with no loss of current capability** — this epic is
  the verification of that requirement (Auto Rag validation is out of scope
  per Staff Engineer Input; it moves to RHAISTRAT-7824).
- **AC-4 (P1): scoped appropriately for multi-tenant environments** —
  per-namespace isolation verified as part of the same campaign.
- **AC-5 (P2, bundled): lightweight enough for resource-constrained
  environments** — bundled because resource-sizing validation is part of the
  same benchmark campaign and report as AC-2; splitting would duplicate the
  instrumented runs. The P2 label reads as relative value, not a deferral
  signal.
